newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt sees Telstra vote on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt sees Telstra vote on Thursday.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it expected the upper house of parliament, the Senate, to vote on a bill for the partial sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp later on Thursday.
"It's time to bring the bill on," government Senate leader Robert Hill told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"There's no reason why we can't get to a vote today and conclude the matter."
Hill said the government remained hopeful that the bill would receive Senate approval after months of negotiations with key Independent senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston.

"They've put to us a number of concerns about potential job losses, the need to give regional areas a fair go with the new technologies, assurances on issues of expenditure of the natural heritage trust," he said.
"We think we've reasonably met their requests, but we won't find out for sure until later this morning."
The two senators hold the key to the bill as they are the only possible sources of the two extra votes the government needs to pass any legislation in the non-government dominated Senate.
All other non-government parties are opposed to the bill.
The government plans to raise A$8.0 billion with the sale of one-third of Telstra with A$1.0 billion of the proceeds earmarked for an environment package.
